The client deck was due at six, and at four Binita noticed the growth figure on slide nine: 38 percent. Her own data pull last week had shown 21. Kamal, the account lead, had finalised the slides that morning.
Her first instinct was to message the team: 'Who inflated this?' She didn't. She reopened the source files and rebuilt the calculation step by step. The raw sales data said 21. She checked the other slides; two more numbers were higher than the source.
On a notepad she drew a line down the middle. Left side, KNOWN: slide 9 says 38, source says 21; slides 12 and 14 also differ. Right side, SUSPECTED: changed on purpose? A different data version?
At 4.40 she went to Kamal's desk with the notepad and the source files, and asked which version he had used.

qa.a: She could hold the deck, keep her notes of the known facts and follow the company's process to raise it with someone senior.

qa.q: How might Kamal feel when Binita shows him the notepad?
qa.a: Kamal might feel defensive or embarrassed, but being asked which version he used gives him room to explain or correct it.

Wednesday, 14 Feb, 11 p.m.
Couldn't sleep, so I finally opened the company handbook instead of scrolling. Section 7, 'Speak Up'. There's a confidential ethics line, run by an outside firm, and an email for the compliance team. Retaliation is not allowed, it says in bold. Good.

2 Feb: Bhavna asked me to back-date three delivery receipts. I said no.
7 Feb: saw the same receipts in the system with January dates.

subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
subtype: Approach: confronting the person publicly [Pitfall]
passage:
Monday night.
I did the stupid thing. In the 10 a.m. team call, with the regional head listening, I said, 'Nitin, your vendor quotes are padded and you know it.' I'd seen two quotes that looked high. That's all I had. No figures on my screen, no talk with him first.
Nitin didn't shout. He just went very still and said, 'Send me what you're referring to.' I couldn't. The regional head ended the call early.
By lunch, Nitin had written to the head that he felt publicly accused. By evening, my own manager was asking why I hadn't come to her first. And now nobody's looking at the quotes. They're looking at me.
If the quotes really are padded, I've made it harder to prove.
Tarun

qa.q: What did Nitin say after going still?
qa.a: 'Send me what you're referring to.'

qa.q: What is Tarun feeling on Monday night?
qa.a: Tarun feels embarrassed and regretful, aware that the outburst moved attention from the quotes to Tarun.

qa.q: What would you change first if you were Tarun?
qa.a: Gather the two quotes and compare them with market prices, then raise it privately with the manager before any meeting.

qa.q: What was the call like for Nitin?
qa.a: Nitin felt publicly accused in front of the regional head, which made him guarded and pushed him to complain.

grounding: It shows an employee accusing a senior colleague in a team call without evidence or prior talk, making him defensive and undermining the concern.
